# Build system

`dashboards.json` is the source of truth for the marketing-dashboards directory
and the reporting-tools hub. **Do not hand-edit generated pages** — edit the
catalog and rebuild.

## Generated by `build.py`

- `marketing-dashboards/<category>/index.html` (10 pages)
- `reporting-tools/index.html`
- `sitemap.xml`, `robots.txt`

Everything else in the repo is still hand-maintained.

## Commands

```bash
python3 build/build.py --out .        # regenerate into the repo
python3 build/verify.py               # semantic diff vs the committed pages
python3 build/pixdiff.py              # headless render + pixel diff
python3 build/extract.py              # re-derive the catalog from the pages
```

`extract.py` only needs re-running if pages are edited by hand — which they
shouldn't be. It exists because it is how the catalog was originally built,
and it documents the migration.

## Catalog shape

`entries[]` — one per dashboard card:

| field | meaning |
|---|---|
| `id`, `category`, `position` | identity and ordering within the category |
| `name`, `vendor`, `blurb`, `tags` | card copy |
| `url` | outbound destination |
| `link_type` | `individual` \| `gallery` \| `blog_post` \| `vendor_homepage` |
| `triage_note` | why it was classified that way |
| `duplicate_of` | set when another card points at the same URL |
| `price_tier` | Free / Free* / Paid / … as shown on the badge |
| `screenshot`, `alt` | Phase 2: self-hosted image; falls back to `image_src` |
| `image_src` | the original hotlinked image, kept until re-shot |
| `placeholder` | key into `placeholders` (14 shared SVGs, deduped from 60) |
| `*_style` | captured inline styles, so regeneration is faithful |

`reporting_tools[]` drives the hub. `static_pages[]` / `blog_posts[]` feed the sitemap.

## Verification

`verify.py` compares meaning (metadata, headings, prose, every card field)
between the committed pages and a fresh build. `INTENTIONAL` in that file lists
content we deliberately changed; anything else that differs is a regression.

`pixdiff.py` renders both and compares pixels. Three pages differ on purpose
because the generator repairs a defect — see `EXPECTED` in that file.
